text:
Miro Heiskanen is back. He left the Nov. 3 game against Washington after under ten minutes, missed five straight, and returned Tuesday in Vegas with a goal and 26:42 of ice time in the Stars' overtime comeback win. Before the absence, he was doing what he always does: four games of 29-plus minutes in his last ten.

The Stars are much better with him. They have 57% of the expected goals with Heiskanen on at five on five, eight points better than without him, and his skating still ranks with the league's best (96th percentile top speed). Twelve points in 16 games is a little below his usual playmaking pace, but the chances around him are where they should be.

His goals are the thing that won't last: four on 1.9 expected, a 14.8% shooting rate against the 7% we'd expect for him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him shooting a lot last season but not often from the slot. Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among defensemen at 2.7 wins, much of it on the power play.
